items.title: Slide Hampton — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: I used to go down and listen to them all the time, because, for all of us that are arrangers, Thad Jones is a phenomenon.

ctx.x: Once again, looping back: Thad Jones–Mel Lewis Big Band. How did you become involved with that project and with the principals there?

I used to go down and listen to them all the time, because, for all of us that are arrangers, Thad Jones is a phenomenon. The way he writes music is impossible. You don’t even try to learn to write music like that. You try to learn to write music as many ways as you can, but you don’t try to learn to write the way that he writes it, because Thad could talk to you right now and write music while he’s doing this interview. When you finish the interview, he might have finished the whole arrangement. This is…
What was your first encounter with Thad? In what circumstance?
